Mission purpose Build a large, authoritative, advisory source base from this review so three independent methods can later build galaxy-evolution wiki pages from zero. Scientific scope 1. Why galaxy-formation models require resolved inflow/outflow accounting and subresolution models. 2. The multiphase ISM: density/temperature structure, cooling and heating, molecular gas, turbulence, gravity, and cloud formation/disruption. 3. Star-formation laws and efficiencies from cloud to galactic scales; how cosmological models implement them. 4. Stellar feedback channels: photoionization, radiation pressure, stellar winds, supernovae, cosmic rays, and their scale coupling. 5. Superbubbles, galactic fountains, winds, mass loading, metal transport, recycling, and the ISM-CGM interface. 6. Numerical methods, resolution, convergence, overcooling, stochastic/thermal/kinetic injection, delayed cooling, decoupled winds, and explicit-feedback models. 7. Model successes and degeneracies: what galaxy statistics were calibrated, what was predicted, and what remained non-unique. 8. Observational benchmarks for gas, star formation, outflows, baryon conversion efficiency, and CGM reservoirs. 9. Bounded discussion of black-hole feedback only where the review treats it as a galaxy-scale model ingredient; no AGN microphysics harvest. Required output 1. Review identity and scope map - Confirm title, authors, year, journal, DOI, arXiv, and ADS bibcode. - Map the scientific territory the review covers. - State what the source base authorizes and what it does not. - Preserve distinctions among observation, analytic theory, simulation, and review synthesis. 2. Established findings - At least 12 atomic entries. - Give IDs [REV04-E01], [REV04-E02], ... - For every entry include: - role: established - epistemic_type: observation | analytic_theory | hydrodynamic_simulation | semi_analytic_model | calibration | review_synthesis - one bounded finding - mass, redshift, phase, environmental, numerical, and/or resolution boundary - review section/topic basis - confidence note - source keys - Do not turn a successful calibrated prescription into proof of a unique mechanism. 3. Open debates and tensions - At least 8 entries with IDs [REV04-D01], ... - Include competing positions, why unresolved in 2017, relevant model/observational boundaries, and source keys. - Include: star-formation efficiency control; dominant stellar-feedback channels; thermal versus kinetic coupling; explicit versus effective feedback; wind mass loading and recycling; cosmic-ray and magnetic support; physical versus numerical convergence; and calibration degeneracy. 4. Include only values you can bind to a cited source and review context. 5. What remained unknown in 2017 - At least 6 entries with IDs [REV04-U01], ... - State the gap, why it matters, and the observation/model/numerical test needed. 6. Primary-citation harvest - Harvest 40-80 important PRIMARY papers actually cited by Naab & Ostriker 2017. - Prefer primary observations, analytic theory, controlled numerical experiments, hydrodynamic simulations, and model implementations. - Supporting reviews may be listed separately but must not count toward the primary total. - Exclude post-2017 papers, uncited search results, source aggregators, and AGN-microphysics papers from usable rows. - One physical paper per source key; no duplicate physical paper under multiple keys. - Use IDs [REV04-P001], [REV04-P002], ... - Each row must be: [REV04-PNNN] Authors (year, journal) | title=exact title | DOI:value-or-none; arXiv:value-or-none; ADS:value | role=measurement|analytic_theory|hydrodynamic_simulation|semi_analytic_model|calibration | review_locator=section/topic | one-line boundary - Cite the exact review location where practical. - If an identifier is uncertain, put the row in DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED, not the usable harvest.
